title: Request ability to hide/show the default wallpapers located under usr/share/wallpapers under wallpaper type image view
line: The Image wallpaper list now has a "Show System Wallpapers" option, so you can see only your own wallpapers.
explanation: The Image wallpaper picker lists every wallpaper it finds, sorted by name, so the ones shipped in /usr/share/wallpapers are mixed in with the user's own (added with Add…, downloaded with Get New…, or placed in ~/.local/share/wallpapers), and the only way to get rid of them was deleting system files. The change adds a checkable "Show System Wallpapers" item to the Images header's overflow menu, stored as a new ShowSystemWallpapers wallpaper setting (default on). When it is off, the list only shows the user's wallpapers (the same ones that already get a Remove button) plus the wallpaper currently in use, so the selection never disappears.

commits.message:
wallpapers/image: add an option to hide system wallpapers

The image list mixes the wallpapers installed with the system with the
user's own ones, and there was no way to see only the latter. Add a
"Show System Wallpapers" toggle to the list's menu, keeping the one in use.

BUG: 515292

media.caption: Before: the user's "Beach Sunset" sits between Plasma's own wallpapers, with no way to hide them
After: with Show System Wallpapers unchecked, only the user's wallpapers are listed
After: if the wallpaper in use is a system one (Evening Glow), it stays listed and selected
After: the option lives in the Images list's menu and is remembered after OK
